name: Water Management & Irrigation

objectives.text: Identify ways plants get water, such as rain, watering cans, and hoses
Describe what happens to a plant that gets too little or too much water
Describe how roots take up water from the soil and move it through the plant
Explain how mulch and shading help a garden bed hold water longer
Use a rain gauge and a simple soil moisture check to decide whether a garden needs watering
Compare drip, sprinkler, and furrow irrigation by how they deliver water and how much water they lose
Explain how the water cycle supplies soil moisture and water for irrigation
Identify common sources of irrigation water such as wells, rivers, ponds, and municipal supplies
Assemble a simple drip irrigation system for a school garden or greenhouse bench using emitters, filters, pressure regulators, and backflow preventers
Describe soil water terms including field capacity, plant available water, permanent wilting point, and gravitational water
Explain how soil texture changes how often and how much a crop should be irrigated
Describe where irrigation fits among the steps of crop production from land preparation through harvest
Describe the effects of irrigation water quality, including pH and dissolved solids, on plant growth
Analyze how interactions between groundwater and surface water affect the water available for irrigation
Analyze plant responses to drought stress and overwatering in a crop or greenhouse setting
Explain how drainage practices such as drain tile, surface drainage, and growing media porosity affect water in the root zone
Use tensiometers or soil moisture sensors to monitor soil water and decide when to irrigate
Calculate a crop's irrigation needs using evapotranspiration and soil moisture data
Measure the application rate and distribution uniformity of a sprinkler or drip system and adjust it for even watering
Interpret electroconductivity and pH results to adjust irrigation practices such as leaching salts from the root zone
Recommend modifications to irrigation water such as acidification or filtration for desired plant growth
Evaluate the economic and environmental tradeoffs of irrigation methods, including energy costs, water rights, and runoff
Design an efficient irrigation system and schedule for a production setting or SAE, justifying the choices made to conserve water

changes: Kept all six existing objectives, rewording some, and moved the water cycle objective to grade 7. Added early objectives on signs of too little or too much water, using mulch to hold water, and rain gauge checks. Added hands-on drip system assembly and system calibration for SAE and greenhouse work. Added high school objectives on soil water terms, how texture affects irrigation, water quality, groundwater and surface water, plant water stress, drainage, moisture sensors, EC and pH adjustments, water treatment, and irrigation tradeoffs. Soil formation, fertility, and conservation topics are left to the sibling sub-topics.
